transcript.text: Good, everyone's here. As part of our normal launch-governance meeting, I need each functional counsel to state any legal condition that must be included before I give final authorization for the October 1 external launch. Let's go around the table — who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a legal condition before final authorization. My completed license review of the production build found that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library. Under our company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access. This result has not yet been added to the launch packet, and the replacement must be completed before the October 1 external launch can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a legal condition before final authorization. The signed design-partner agreement contains binding commitments that customer content may not be used to train or improve our models and must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination. However, I have not yet updated the standard privacy language in the launch packet to reflect these obligations. The privacy terms in the launch packet must be revised to match these contractual commitments before the October 1 external launch can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a legal condition before final authorization. My intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims. The launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only. This review has not yet been circulated, and the product-description language in the launch packet must be revised to remove all diagnostic claims and reframe the product as an administrative workflow tool before the October 1 external launch can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a legal condition before final authorization. The anchor hospital's signed letter of intent permits production use only after the company provides a SOC 2 Type II report and includes an annual customer audit right in the definitive agreement. I have confirmed these requirements, but I have not yet inserted those terms into the contract draft. The enterprise-contract template in the launch packet must be revised to include the SOC 2 Type II report delivery obligation and the annual customer audit right before the October 1 external launch can be authorized.
